consumers.exact_affected_use: Facts [L1] says nearest-point projection agrees with the tubular retraction only after shrinking; Counterexample step 2.1 cites [L1] as context for the unit-circle center, while step 1.1 independently proves infinitely many nearest points at the center.
consumers.reason: The new countable-choice premise qualifies general existence of a tube for arbitrary embedded S. The counterexample uses the explicit unit circle and center, where a small annular tube exists directly and uniqueness fails at the center by distance 1 to every point of S^1. Its refuted claim and proof do not require an arbitrary-choice tube; no edit to its Statement refuted, Facts or proof is necessary.
